title: The Perfect Match
intro: You matched with someone on a dating app. The conversation is lovely, and then it moves quickly.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

notify.text: Let us move to the messaging app 💕

msg.text: Let us move to the messaging app
I think I am falling for you already.
I am shy about photos and calls, we will talk by text.

special.label: Instant flattery
special.why: Fast flattery is a way to lower your guard.

move.label: Move off the app quickly
move.lens: They want you away from the app's safety tools.
move.why: Scammers move you to private chat fast.

nopic.label: No photos or calls
nopic.why: A person who never appears on camera may not be real.

actions.label: Move to the messaging app and keep chatting
Ask for a video call first, and stay on the app
Stop chatting and report the profile

block_report.line: You reported the profile. The app removed it before it reached more people.

verify.line: You asked for a video call. The profile gave excuses and vanished. Case cracked.

go_ahead.line: The "match" became a close friend in a week, then needed money for an emergency.

what_if.go_ahead: Insisting on a video call, and staying on the app, were the exits. Love does not rush you off a safe app.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting it as well helps protect other people.

golden_rule: A match who flatters you fast and moves you off the app is a warning. Ask for a video call, and report if they refuse.

quick_check.q: A new match flatters you, says they are falling for you and wants to move to a private app. What do you do?

options.text: Stay on the app, ask for a video call, and report if they refuse
Send a photo to build trust

quick_check.explain: Fast love and a fast move are the pattern.

hints.nudge: How fast did the love arrive, and where do they want to chat?

rows.k: Will they do a video call?
Pressure to move off the platform
